summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on fraud/security, regulation.

articles.title: Sezzle pivots to national bank charter
articles.description: With states imposing tighter rules on buy now, pay later companies, Sezzle CEO Charlie Youakim views a federal charter as “the most robust solution.”

articles.title: Cash lags credit, debit payments
articles.description: Though most consumers prefer debit and credit card payments, 90% say they’ll still use cash for the foreseeable future, a Fed survey finds.

articles.title: Fiserv seeks investor lawsuit dismissal
articles.description: Shareholders angry over the stock’s decline are alleging fraud with a complaint that has no merit, the payment processor said in its response.

articles.title: States lean in on payments plays
articles.description: States are taking a larger role to regulate emerging payments offerings, like earned wage access and buy now, pay later. How will that unfold? Here is the perspective of one lawyer who worked for California state government.

articles.title: Shift4 racked by Iran turmoil
articles.description: The payments processor sees a large opportunity to expand merchant services sales within its Global Blue retail network, CEO Taylor Lauber said.

articles.title: Senate passes cash-rounding bill
articles.description: If enacted, the new law would provide a federal framework for how to round cash retail transactions as pennies grow scarce.

articles.title: FedNow extension wins support
articles.description: Stripe, Visa, Wise and industry trade groups back the Federal Reserve’s plan to expand its instant payment system for cross-border use.

articles.title: Visa debit case turns on market definition, lawyers say
articles.description: The card network will argue that the DOJ’s view of the debit card market is too narrow, legal experts predicted as the case heads toward trial.
